title: Autofix engine: act on unit-failure events
description: Connect systemd unit-failure events (already subscribed via monitors -> services JobRemoved) to the remediation tier using the act/ask matrix: safe+reversible -> auto-remediate with undo-after; else the one rare push. Plumbing exists; policy does not. See docs/ux.md.

title: Tray menu + live updates
description: Menu: status line + failed units, each a Fix-it action -> remediation (which confirms/verifies). Refresh icon+menu from daemon Events and when a unit clears.
close_reason: Per-unit fix-it menu rows (Restart <unit>) via new structured RestartUnit protocol message — deterministic, no NL round-trip; daemon acts only on units it currently reports failed, scope taken from its live view. Live updates via event-driven + post-fix refresh. Factored restart_resolved out of remediation.run.

title: nixadmin-tray: SNI item via dbus-fast

close_reason: SNI tray via dbus-fast: green/amber/grey disc icon, health from daemon ListFailures, DBusMenu status header + Quit, re-registers on host restart. Validated live against cosmic-applet-status-area.

title: Daemon: structured list-failed-units query
description: A protocol query returning failed units as structured data (name, reason, scope system/user) so a client renders per-unit actions, instead of parsing the services fetcher text.
notes: Done on feat/tray. Protocol: ListFailures (client->daemon) + Failures (daemon->client) carrying structured {unit, scope, description} entries. remediation.failed_units() gathers failed .service units across system+user scopes. server._list_failures handles the request. Protocol round-trip tests incl. the list-of-dict field + empty case. nix flake check green.

title: Remediation: route system-unit fix through the helper
description: Extend remediation.py so restarting a failed SYSTEM unit goes via the helper restart action; user units already work. Keep confirm+verify+honest-report.
notes: Done on feat/tray. remediation.run is now scope-aware: gathers system+user units, restarts user units directly and SYSTEM units via injected restart_system (safety.apply_restart -> helper restart action from gav.1); confirm+verify+honest-report preserved, scope-appropriate is-failed/journal-tail. safety: generalized _run_helper to a request dict; added apply_restart(unit). server wires restart_system. Tests: apply_restart protocol (fake helper) + system-scope routing (mocked). nix flake check green. Live end-to-end validation bundled with the backend deploy.

title: Helper: privileged restart <unit> action
description: Add a restart action to nixadmin-helper.py so system units can be restarted via the root helper; validate the unit name; sits alongside the rebuild actions. The one backend gap. Subsumes the generic issue nix-nixadmin-s01.
notes: Code complete on feat/tray: restart action + valid_unit (deny-list + charset/suffix), _run_restart (direct systemctl restart, watchdog), protocol doc. Unit tests for valid_unit; helper flake8 + nix flake check green. Live restart validation bundled with the gav.2 backend deploy (needs a helper-changing switch).

title: PoC: supervised systemd-failure tray
description: First UI increment. An SNI tray item (native to COSMIC status-area via dbus-fast, verified: org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher hosted by cosmic-applet-status-area) that shows overall health and lists failed systemd units in its DBusMenu, each with a Fix-it (restart) action, wired to existing detection (monitors/JobRemoved) + remediation. Supervised mode: human approves each fix; manual precursor to the autofix engine. Inc1=tray+fix (no web). Inc2=Open-detail web view. Design: docs/ux.md. Defers libcosmic-vs-GTK.

title: Find a better project name + discoverable AI text
description: Rename the project — 'nixadmin' is techy and admin-centric. The name should encode the relationship/trust (see vision.md: 'caring distribution', 'a computer you can give to someone you love'), not the capability. SEPARATELY and intentionally: add AI keywords to the DISCOVERABILITY text (repo description, README, package metadata, topics) so people searching for AI tools can find it — that is how this category is discovered today. The tension is deliberate and resolved by PLACEMENT: 'AI' lives in searchable metadata, NOT in the name or the UI. The product mission stays design-for-silence (ux.md) — AI is an implementation detail, never foregrounded in the experience. Document WHY the AI text exists (findability) so nobody later removes it thinking it violates the no-AI-in-focus principle.

title: LLM-inferred remediation (propose, never execute)
description: Beyond restart: LLM infers the LIKELY remediation from failure + live state, and flags when a restart WON'T help (config error, disk full) -> steers to the real fix (prevents futile-restart trust erosion). GUARDRAILS (keep translator-never-actor): (1) LLM PROPOSES from a bounded catalog of safe deterministic actions, or proposes a config edit through worktree-validate->confirm->verify->rollback; NEVER emits a command to run (judge over real candidates, like the action tier). (2) Deterministic-first: detect remediation class without the LLM where possible (disk full->df, restart-loop->NRestarts, stuck queue->cups state); LLM judges only the ambiguous residue. (3) Confidence+reversibility gate autonomy: restart=auto/offer; inferred fix=offer-as-hypothesis+confirm; novel=escalate to frontier+change tier. (4) Inference is a hypothesis, verified after acting; never fake confidence.

title: LLM-humanized failure explanation (on-demand)
description: First LLM role in the tray: translate raw state -> plain language. Menu label stays DETERMINISTIC (e.g. 'Bluetooth - stopped'; works cold). Detail/Explain invokes the LLM lazily (name-why-fix; reuses the #1 diagnosis pipeline). LLM = translator machine->human, never the actor. Eager-vs-lazy: PoC is lazy (raw until Explain); consider eager-on-failure later since failures are rare.
notes: Decided: LAZY via an explicit 'Explain' button (per failure or overall). Click -> fires the LLM to refine/humanize the raw error; raw stays visible (deterministic, works cold). Reuses the #1 diagnosis pipeline (name-why-fix on the clicked unit) -> mostly wiring. UX: click -> Status('warming up…') -> explanation streams (Delta) over the raw, so the ~6s cold-load feels responsive. Doubles as a prompt-iteration testbed (compare raw vs explained).
